definition: Sensory amusia is a loss of the ability to understand or appreciate music. It is described as a musical disorder parallel to sensory language impairment and may occur even when aphasia is absent.

provenance.revision: 1901 New York Macmillan original; archive index checked 2026-10-18
provenance.scope: Source record Amusia; pinned source text

reasons: “sensory language impairment” is not supported by the packet; the source says amusia is analogous to aphasia in regard to speech, not to a sensory language-impairment category.

The definition slightly paraphrases the source in a way that adds an unsupported framing of the condition as a “musical disorder” parallel to another named impairment; the packet supports only the historical analogy to aphasia and the specific sensory form as loss of comprehension/appreciation of music.
The sense is otherwise correct, but the unsupported comparison means the definition does not fully pass as written.

The definition claims sensory amusia is “parallel to sensory language impairment,” but the packet does not use that wording or concept; it instead says amusia is analogous to aphasia “in regard to speech.”

Aside from that mismatch, the remaining elements are supported by the packet (sensory amusia as loss of comprehension/appreciation of music, and that sensory and amnesic amusia can occur without aphasia).
